images.caption: View from Thomas Street through the arch which forms the main entrance to the National College of Art and Design (there are big blue arch doors, open during office hours, with a postern door, perhaps for night access).  The line of the view is Dukes Lane, the main internal "street" of the college, with the School of Fine Art on one side, some central buildings and Red Square on the other, and the School of Design off to the right.

images.filename: NCAD, Dublin, facade on Thomas Street, looking east.jpg
images.caption: A "working" view of the long main façade of the National College of Art and Design complex, Thomas Street, Dublin, looking east.  The complex has an internal street and yard landscape, and the buildings on Thomas Street account for less than half the academic and office space.  The main entrance is not the grand brown door, which is a largely unused entrance to the NCAD Gallery, but a blue-doored arch.
images.alt: A "working" view of the long main façade of the National College of Art and Design complex, Thomas Street, Dublin, looking east.  The complex has an internal street and yard landscape, and the buildings on Thomas Street account for less than half the academic and office space.  The main entrance is not the grand brown door, which is a largely unused entrance to the NCAD Gallery, but a blue-doored arch.
